A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Spectral Image Tokenizer by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet reconstruction experiments, MS-COCO generation and upsampling results, editing examples, and tokenizer ablations.

after.justification: V2 reports original reconstruction and text-conditioned generation results, revised ablations, and new class-conditional ImageNet generation experiments at 256×256 and 512×512.

M1.justification: Section 4 replaces separate transformer parameters and codebooks for every scale with approximation-versus-details groups; AR token embeddings and prediction heads change accordingly. V1's entropy regularizer is removed from the stated objective. The new AR-SIT-4* variant additionally introduces GeGLU, axial 2D RoPE, and scale-dependent loss weighting.

E1.justification: V2 adds class-conditional ImageNet generation at 256×256 and 512×512 in Section 5.5. ImageNet previously supported reconstruction experiments only. ImageNet, WebLI, and MS-COCO remain the datasets; 512×512 reconstruction and 16×16-input upsampling already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: V2 Table 3 introduces class-conditional comparisons against AR-ViT-VQGAN, RQ-VAE, DQ-VAE, LlamaGen-L, and VAR. Several were discussed in v1 but had no reported comparison against SIT. V2 Table 1 also adds a reproduced ViT-VQGAN row alongside the reported and no-logit-laplace baselines.

E3.justification: The reported reconstruction configuration changes from Base transformers with 12 layers and 768-dimensional features to Small transformers with 8 layers and 512-dimensional features. Table 2's generation hardware changes from TPU v5e to v6e. New class-conditional protocols introduce 650M and 350M configurations, different guidance settings, and training budgets detailed in Appendix B.3.

E4.justification: Appendix A and Table 5 substantially replace the ablation design. V1 tests entropy regularization, codebook sharing, transformer parameter sharing, and model size. V2 adds vocabulary-size, sequence-length, and Haar/LeGall5/3/CDF9/7 comparisons while removing those component ablations and retaining only part of the scale-causal attention study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Results remain scalar estimates without reported uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace many results under revised model or hardware settings; for example, 256×256 AR-SIT-SCD-4 FID changes from 13.7 to 12.6, which is not a controlled cross-version gain. New results include AR-SIT-4 FID 6.95 at 256×256 and AR-SIT-5* FID 5.97 at 512×512. V2 omits the former 512×512 SIT-4 result and the lowest-resolution baseline FIDs. Table 4's upsampling scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 revises the formal quantizer definition from scale-specific Q_s to separate approximation and details mappings, and removes the defined entropy regularizers. The DWT background, patchification equations, and autoregressive likelihood reasoning remain substantively unchanged; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and six central multiscale properties retain their meaning. The conclusion changes from acknowledging highest-resolution AR generation underperformance to claiming similar text-to-image performance and improved class-conditional generation. This extends the performance claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds explanations for reconstruction–generation tradeoffs and hypothesizes that larger wavelet supports cause padding and interpatch information leakage. Section 5.5 qualifies broader baseline comparisons through architectural and training differences, including VAR's larger tokenizer training dataset. These extend the retained spectral and multiscale interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds extensive implementation information for the class-conditional variants, including dimensions, dropout, vocabulary size, learning rates, loss weights, batch sizes, training duration, and adversarial-training onset. Appendix B.1 revises reconstruction specifications. Appendix B.2 newly discloses guidance scale 3.0 and no reranking for text-to-image generation; this disclosure alone does not establish a procedural change.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds targeted discussion of FAR, DQ-VAE, QG-VAE, and SEMANTICIST. Appendix A connects the new analyses to additional compression–generation and wavelet literature. The central positioning—operating on input DWT coefficients rather than learned latent features—remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and much of the prose are retained. V2 labels the introductory properties P.1–P.6 and cross-references them, introduces ADTransformer terminology, merges high-resolution reconstruction into Section 5.1, and reorganizes the implementation appendix. These are localized editorial and structural revisions.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn for approximation/details parameter sharing. Table 1 incorporates the former high-resolution Table 3, while a new class-conditional Table 3 and Figures 9–10 are introduced. Table 5 is substantially redesigned, several sample grids are replaced, and retained appendix figures are reordered and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the empirical case beyond v1's narrow generative comparisons. It adds a matched class-conditional comparison—FID 6.95 versus the reproduced baseline's 8.37—broader comparisons with explicit limitations, and actual 512×512 generation where v1 demonstrated only reconstruction. New sensitivity analyses and detailed implementation specifications improve interpretability and reproducibility. Some direct component ablations are lost, and changed settings prevent simple cross-version performance claims, but the added controlled validation provides a substantial overall benefit.
